requirements.text: The THEMAS system shall control the heating and cooling units that are defined as part of the THEMAS system.
The system shall read this file and the definitions shall be derived from the initialization data in the file.
The THEMAS system shall use the information contained in the initialization data file to determine which heating and cooling units are part of the THEMAS system.
Each thermostat shall have a unique identifier by which that thermostat is identified in the THEMAS system.
The initialization file shall contain a unique identifier for each thermostat that the system is to monitor.
These identifiers shall be read from the initialization file and loaded into the THEMAS system during the initialization process.
There shall be a maximum number of heating or cooling units that can be on at any given time.
The maximum number of concurrently running units shall be read from the initialization file and stored in the THEMAS system.
This procedure shall read the initialization file and establish the trigger value from the data in that file.
The THEMAS system shall ensure the temperature reported by a given thermostat shall not exceed a maximum deviation value of 3 degrees Fahrenheit.
This procedure shall read the initialization file and establish the overtemperature value from the data in that file.
The THEMAS system shall only respond to temperatures that are within a reasonable value.
This procedure shall read the initialization file and establish the valid temperature range from the data in it.
When the THEMAS system is initialized, it shall first turn off all the heating and cooling units.
The THEMAS system shall only respond to temperatures from the thermostats that are within the specified valid range.
The THEMAS system shall determine when a reported temperature or a changed temperature setting exceeds the limits set by the overtemperature values.
When the current temperature value exceeds the current temperature setting by a pre-defined amount, the THEMAS system shall activate the appropriate heating or cooling unit.
The THEMAS system shall limit the number of heating or cooling units that may be running simultaneously.
When a request for a heating unit or cooling to be turned is denied, an event shall be generated and the THEMAS system shall record that event.
The THEMAS system shall control the heating and cooling units that are designated as part of the THEMAS system.
Once a request to turn on or off a heating or cooling unit, the THEMAS system shall provide the necessary control signal for the unit.
For each event that is generated, the THEMAS system shall identify each event and generate the appropriate event data.
The THEMAS system shall provide the supervisor a mechanism to change the temperature setting of any of the thermostats in the system.

The THEMAS shall provide the ability for the supervisor to select between two different types of reports: 1) the operational history of the THEMAS system for the past twelve months and 2) a statistical summary for any selected month.
The THEMAS system shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) requiring authentication for any supervisor-level actions, including changing thermostat settings and generating reports.
The THEMAS system shall validate the integrity of the initialization file using a checksum or digital signature before loading operational parameters to prevent unauthorized system behavior.
The THEMAS system shall define a valid temperature range of -20°F to 130°F; any input outside this range shall be logged as an error and ignored.
The system shall maintain an operational history for a rolling 12-month period; data older than 12 months shall be archived or purged to maintain database performance.
The THEMAS system shall poll all thermostats for current temperature data at a frequency of at least once every 5 seconds.
The THEMAS system shall generate the 12-month operational history report within 30 seconds of the supervisor's request.
The THEMAS system shall trigger the audible alarm within 1 second of detecting an invalid temperature or overtemperature condition.

OPEN: The system lacks requirements for protecting the integrity and confidentiality of the event database stored on the supervisor's computer. - The THEMAS system shall ensure that event data stored in the Microsoft Access database is protected against unauthorized modification and unauthorized access through file-system level permissions or database encryption.

OPEN: The system lacks a defined recovery strategy or timeout mechanism for when the 'TBD' signal interface fails to communicate with heating/cooling units. - The system shall implement a watchdog timer for H/C unit signals; if a signal is not acknowledged within 500ms, the system shall log a critical failure event and retry up to 3 times.

OPEN: The LIFO queue for H/C requests lacks a defined maximum depth, which could lead to memory exhaustion or stale request processing. - The LIFO queue shall have a maximum capacity of 100 requests; requests exceeding this limit shall be dropped and logged as a system overflow event.

OPEN: The system capacity for the number of thermostats and heating/cooling units is not defined, making it impossible to size the system or validate performance under load. - The THEMAS system shall support a minimum of 12 thermostats and 12 heating/cooling units as specified in the building layout.
